title: Understand Statistical Questions
objective: I can tell the difference between a statistical question and a non-statistical question.
model: sorting questions by whether their answers are expected to vary, supported by dot plots and tables of collected answers

widgets.where: Practice §1 (4 items: 2 mc on dot plots, 1 num on a frequency table, 1 mc on list of answers)
widgets.component: Dive Prep: read a dot plot and a table of answers, count different answers
widgets.root: Checked each key against its data: dot plot [1,2,2,3,3,3,5,5,6,8] has 2 dots at 5; table 3+8+6+1 = 18 nests; greatest dot 45; 0,1,2,5 are 4 different answers. Builds the data/variability reading 2-1 needs.

widgets.component: Which question is (not) statistical, and why
widgets.root: Each item turns on 'do the answers vary across cases'; distractors trap topic, numeric answer and who asked. Keys verified.

widgets.component: Sort questions into statistical / one fixed answer
widgets.root: Card bins are correct (each swimmer height, laps per runner statistical; mascot colour, players on a team fixed). Classification is the lesson's skill and sorting makes the student commit to each case.

widgets.component: Spot the faulty reason in a statistical-question decision
widgets.root: Both reasons ('height is one number', 'a sports topic and a number make it statistical') are the lesson's named misconceptions and the fixes are right.

widgets.where: Practice §4 (7 pooled items: mc, sort, match, num, err, tbl, dot plots)
widgets.component: Fresh pooled questions with dot plots and answer lists
widgets.root: Read all 14 pool items: classification keys correct; the stop-sign dot plot (nine dots at 8) and the two-team urchin counts 8,8,8,8,8 vs 3,9,6,12,5 are real variability contrasts.

Keys correct, wrong-answer feedback names the misconception. Note 5.3 repeats 3.4 and 5.4 repeats 2.1 almost verbatim (one mc stem used four times in the studio); harmless to correctness but it re-tests memory of the stem.

widgets.where: Challenge §1 (6 pooled items), §2 items 1-7, §3 items 1-3, §4 items 1-4, §5 items 1-6
widgets.component: Climb, missions, sorts, matches, error analysis, counting data values, write-your-own
widgets.root: Spot-checked all counts (14 divers x 3 dives = 42; 24 + 1 = 25 values; 6 teams) and the err items: 'a total is one answer', 'one boat measured monthly varies', 'each week has 7 days' are all right. Variability sort (no/low/high) and match-the-statistical-partner go beyond recognition.

typography: Practice §5 item 5 distractor reads 'How many pages are in a standard dictionary page?' (garbled; should be 'How many pages are in a standard dictionary?')
